question.text: The position–time (x–t) plots for two bodies, A and B, traveling along the x-axis are straight lines. At time t = 0 s, body A is located at x = 10 m while body B is at the origin (x = 0 m). At t = 5 s, both bodies reach x = 12 m. Determine the velocity of body A relative to body B.
conditions: position of A at t = 0 s is 10 m
position of B at t = 0 s is 0 m
both particles are at x = 12 m at t = 5 s

figure.description: A position versus time (x–t) graph showing position x in meters on the vertical axis and time t in seconds on the horizontal axis. Particle A's straight-line trajectory begins at (0 s, 10 m), while particle B's straight-line trajectory begins at the origin (0 s, 0 m). The two lines intersect at the coordinates (5 s, 12 m).

solution.approach: The slope of each x-t line is that particle's velocity, and the relative velocity is the difference of the two velocities.

steps.text: Find the velocity of A from the slope of its line using the two given points, (t = 0, x = 10 m) and (t = 5 s, x = 12 m).
Find the velocity of B from the slope of its line using the two given points, (t = 0, x = 0) and (t = 5 s, x = 12 m).
Velocity of A with respect to B is the vector difference of the two velocities.
steps.why_this_step: Both lines are straight, so each slope is a constant velocity, and the relative velocity is also constant.

common_mistakes.text: Subtracting in the wrong order, v_B − v_A, gives +2 m/s instead of −2 m/s.
Reading A's slope from the intersection point without the 10 m starting offset, as 12/5 = 2.4 m/s, gives v_AB = 0 instead of −2 m/s.
